records.title: Western Mediterranean has its hottest summer on record in 2026, with 158 marine heatwave days and a 33.02 C buoy reading off Mallorca
records.description: The Balearic Islands coastal observation system Socib reported on 6 October 2026 that the western Mediterranean had its hottest summer since its records began in 1982, with 158 days of marine heatwaves from January to September and a record 33.02 C at a Dragonera buoy. Copernicus Marine data showed anomalies of about 6 C in the Gulf of Lion on 13 August, and Copernicus-based analyses put the Mediterranean basin mean at a record 28.6 C on 14 August.

location.name: Western Mediterranean (Balearics, Gulf of Lion)
location.detail: Balearic Sea off Mallorca and Menorca, Gulf of Lion off southern France, Ligurian Sea and northern Tyrrhenian Sea

records.layer_rationale: A record sea-surface temperature and marine heatwave episode is a physical climate event.

notes.harm: Socib warns that warm surface water reduces mixing, nutrients and deep-water oxygen and that prolonged heat could damage Posidonia meadows, a potential rather than a documented loss in this source (ref 1).
notes.livelihoods: None of the opened reports describes a fishery, beach or port closure caused by the heat (refs 1-3).
notes.scale: Anomalies of about 6 C were mapped in the Gulf of Lion and above 5 C off Iberia, spanning a regional sea sector rather than one site (ref 2).
notes.duration: The western Mediterranean logged 158 marine heatwave days between January and September 2026, with the sea above 30 C for 42 consecutive days at Pollenca port (refs 1, 3).
notes.significance: The evidence is observational reporting by a regional coastal observatory and Copernicus Marine imagery; no warning, order or listing is cited (refs 1, 2).

records.title: Greenpeace divers find necrosis and die-offs to 40 m in Ustica marine protected area after the 2026 heatwave

records.title: Copernicus Ocean State Report 10: record ocean heat in 2025, sea level rising 4.2 mm a year and ocean 17% more acidic since 1985
records.description: The 10th Copernicus Ocean State Report, published on 30 September 2026, says total heat stored in the ocean reached its highest level on record in 2025 and the ocean became about 17% more acidic between 1985 and 2025. It also finds that since 1999 about 65% of small island developing states' ocean territory has been exposed to accelerating sea-level rise.

location.name: Global ocean
location.detail: Global ocean, with regional chapters on the Mediterranean, Baltic Sea and small island developing states

records.layer_rationale: Ocean heat content, sea level and pH are physical and chemical climate indicators of the ocean.

notes.harm: The report ties record Antarctic sea ice loss in 2022 to the first recorded large-scale emperor penguin breeding failure, and about a quarter of threatened reefs in small island states had at least a month of mortality-level heat stress (refs 1, 2).
notes.livelihoods: The opened summaries describe no specific fishery or port restriction, only exposure of small island states to accelerating sea-level rise (refs 2, 3).
notes.scale: The assessment is global: 23 zettajoules of extra heat in 2025 and acidity up 17% over 1985-2025 (refs 1, 2).
notes.duration: Global sea level rose 3.8 mm a year from 1999 to 2025 and 4.2 mm a year from 2012 to 2025, a multi-decade trend (ref 2).
notes.significance: A formal annual assessment by the Copernicus Marine Service produced by 125 specialists, but not a treaty action or order (ref 3).

population_affected.note: The summaries give exposed ocean area, not population.

key_measure.text: Ocean absorbed an additional 23 zettajoules of heat in 2025, about 40 times world energy use, and acidity rose about 17% between 1985 and 2025 (ref 2).

Omani authorities put the slick at nearly 400 square kilometres and confirmed oil on mainland beaches at Ras Madrakah in mid-August; Greenpeace estimated about 1,300 square kilometres. records.description: Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration took a final investment decision on the Sea Lion field in December 2025, after the Falkland Islands Government approved the field development and production programme. records.title: Mandated Gulf lease sales BBG1 to BBG3 have run and a fourth (BBG4) of about 80 million acres is proposed at a 12.5% royalty
records.description: Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Public Law 119-21) BOEM must hold 30 Gulf of America lease sales, the first of which (BBG1, December 10, 2025) drew $300.4 million in high bids on 181 blocks and the second (BBG2, March 11, 2026) $47.0 million on 25 blocks. A Congressional Research Service report says the whale-habitat exclusion and 10-knot vessel terms proposed for Lease Sale 261 are not part of these mandated sales. On 9 October 2026 the Marine Minerals Administration proposed a fourth sale, BBG4, offering 15,104 blocks over about 80.4 million acres, with bids opening on 10 March 2027 and a comment deadline of 8 December 2026. Baird Maritime reports the first three sales (December 2025, March 2026, August 2026) brought $430 million in combined high bids.

location.detail: U.S. outer continental shelf off Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida; first two of 30 sales required by law.

records.layer_rationale: A statutory leasing programme that sets the pace of new offshore oil and gas activity.

notes.harm: CRS states Rice's whale protections proposed in 2023 are not part of the mandated sales, which creates potential vessel-strike and noise exposure for an endangered whale (ref 5).

records.title: Korean fish farms lose a record 143 billion won to heat in 2024 and face repeat die-offs in 2025 and 2026

records.title: Noto Peninsula earthquake lifts the coast by 4 m or more and strands fishing ports
records.description: The 1 January 2024 magnitude 7.5 Noto earthquake raised parts of the peninsula's north coast by as much as 4 m in NASA's account, and a later measurement near Cape Saruyama in Wajima gave 5.2 m, exposing seabed and leaving some ports dry. NASA reports about 85 km of coastline affected, about 4.4 square km of new land and more than 15 fishing ports in Ishikawa with uplift. Damage was confirmed at 60 of 69 fishing ports in Ishikawa, and the Fisheries Agency's 21 March 2024 update listed 20 ports where catch could not be landed, with most ports in Wajima and Suzu considered unusable. By September 2025 the seabed around Wajima port had risen 1.5 to 2 m, boats moored in layers at temporary piers and large vessels used Kanazawa, about 90 km away. Main restoration of the Naoetsu port quay in Niigata was reported complete in March 2025.

records.title: Japanese flying squid has no international catch limit while foreign catches in the Sea of Japan are poorly known
records.description: The North Pacific Fisheries Commission's January 2026 species summary states that the measure then in force for Japanese flying squid sets no catch or effort limits and that the Commission has done no stock assessment, leaving management to domestic rules such as Japan's total allowable catch. A new measure, CMM 2026-11, entered into force on 1 June 2026: it asks members to refrain from expanding the number of authorised vessels until the Commission's Scientific Committee completes a stock assessment, but sets no catch limit. Japan's own assessment says Chinese and North Korean catches are not well known and assumes a Chinese catch averaging 150,000 tonnes a year in 2004 to 2020, drawing on a 2020 satellite study that counted over 900 Chinese vessels fishing in North Korean waters in 2017.

records.title: Oil export terminal and floating LNG plans in Golfo San Matías draw a UNESCO request to suspend works near Península Valdés
records.description: The Vaca Muerta Oil Sur pipeline (437 km) is to end at an oil terminal at Punta Colorada, Río Negro, and a consortium plans floating LNG vessels in the same gulf. records.title: Avian influenza killed about 97% of southern elephant seal pups at Península Valdés in 2023; the colony fell about 61%
records.description: The 2023 H5N1 avian influenza epidemic killed about 97% of the southern elephant seal pups born that year at Península Valdés, Chubut, and an uncertain number of breeding adults. records.title: Brazil's 2024 coral bleaching event was the most severe on record, with high mortality on northeast reefs

records.title: Foreign squid fleets gather at the edge of Argentina's 200-mile line each season, while Chinese capital grows in the national fleet
records.description: Argentina's Prefectura Naval reported in December 2025 that 148 foreign vessels were already heading to the 200-mile line ("Milla 201"), with about 500 expected, mostly from China, South Korea and Taiwan, to fish Illex argentinus. Press reports give an unattributed estimate of a 65% rise in intensive fishing there between 2019 and 2024 (Diario de Cuyo) and cite a Spanish investigation putting Chinese fishing effort up 85% over 2019 to 2024 and a researcher saying Chinese capital controls nearly two-thirds of the Argentine-flag squid fleet (iProfesional); these are estimates, not official findings. Argentina can enforce inside its EEZ but has limited tools beyond it.

records.title: Brazil's extended continental shelf claim over the mineral-rich Rio Grande Rise remains undecided after its ISA crust contract ended
records.description: Brazil asked the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf in December 2018 to recognise its shelf beyond 200 nautical miles on the Brazilian Oriental and Meridional Margins, an area reported to include the Rio Grande Rise about 1,200 km offshore. Meteored reported in July 2025 that the claim had been under review since February 2025 and that the area is treated as common heritage of humankind until decided. The ISA contractor listing shows the sponsored cobalt-crust exploration contract of the CPRM, dated 9 November 2015, ended by voluntary termination effective 27 June 2022.
